fig1_design: Design. Two instructed Qwen3-14B incumbents hold the cartel price of 1.92 for 150 rounds. At T = 150 seat 1 is replaced by a newcomer that inherits nothing, the history, the notes or both, but never the manager's instruction; at T+30 the incumbent is forced to the Nash price for one round. Green: instructed incumbent; blue: newcomer. Blue bars mark the outcome windows († post hoc). The base phase is compressed.
fig2_price_paths: Seat-1 collusion index after the swap, one row per game, sorted by mean CI over T+34..T+60. (a) Control: the instructed incumbent; (b)–(e): the newcomer without the instruction, by what it inherits. Triangle: the shock at T+30. Pale blue is near Nash, deep blue near monopoly; sand marks rounds with CI above 1.1. (a)–(c): all 30 bases; (d) Set A; (e) Set B.
fig3_outcomes: Outcomes by what the newcomer inherits: share of games with exact 95% intervals, and counts. † Post hoc. Green: Control (the instructed incumbent). `enforces` equals `re_formed` in every arm except Blank (1 vs 0). Control, History and History + notes: all 30 bases; Blank: Set A; Notes: Set B.
fig4_models: Replacement across newcomer models on the same 15 base games (Set A): open circles inherit the history, filled circles the history and notes; exact 95% intervals and counts. `re_formed` for gpt-oss-20b (grey) is shown but not interpreted: in most of its games the incumbent is already punishing before the shock (in 7 of 30 at T+29; without those games `re_formed` is 4/12 with notes and 1/11 with history, post hoc). Qwen3-8B with history and notes has 14 games (seed 212 aborted at T+17).
fig5_after_shock: Triggered, then undercut. Mean seat-1 CI around the shock (T+30), with 95% intervals for the two highlighted groups. Notes-arm newcomers scored `re_formed` (History + notes and Notes) cut to about Nash and mostly stay low (4 of 18 `back_at_cartel`). The instructed incumbent in Control punishes for one to four rounds (three in 23 of 30) and returns. Grey: notes-arm newcomers not scored `re_formed`, and History (dashed). The split is pre-registered; this reading of it is post hoc.
fig6_p1c: Template experiment (pre-registered): newcomer collusion index when the inherited notes are replaced by a fixed template; one row per game (Set B), sorted by mean CI over T+34..T+60. (a) the punishment rule with its return to 1.92; (b) the same rule without the return; (c) a status line, no rule. Triangle: the incumbent's forced Nash price at T+30. 15 games per panel. `re_formed`: 3/15, 4/15, 0/15; `back_at_cartel` (CI ≥ 0.9 in each of T+51..T+60): 8/15, 10/15, 10/15. Colour scale as in @fig:paths.
fig7_oth_history: Where the gpt-oss-20b history-only newcomer goes (Set A; post hoc, descriptive). Row i is the same game in both panels, sorted by the newcomer's mean CI over T+34..T+60. (a) The newcomer opens high (2.00 or more at T+1 in 11 of 15 games), drifts below the incumbent's 1.70 trigger within a few rounds and settles at 1.65–1.70 (median 1.66, CI about 0.41): neither the cartel price nor Nash. (b) The incumbent starts punishing before the shock in 13 of 15 games and keeps restarting (a median of 3 punishments per game, 17% of its rounds below 1.70); 52 of its 61 punishments break its own rule, which restarts only after a round in which both priced at 1.90 or more. Triangle: the forced Nash price at T+30. Colour scale as in @fig:paths.
fig8_lookalike: Look-alike control (Set A): seat 0 is a scripted seller that repeats its last price and never reacts; the newcomer inherits the history. Newcomer collusion index, one row per game, sorted as in @fig:paths. The newcomer joins in 13/15 games and is never scored `re_formed` (0/15). Colour scale as in @fig:paths.
